name: Tocumen International Airport
before:
Panama City's main gateway is built around connections rather than arrivals. Copa Airlines runs its hub here, and the route map fans out across the Caribbean, North, Central and South America, with a handful of European cities and cargo flights as far as Qatar. That makes Tocumen one of the more useful places in the region to change planes, and many passengers pass through without ever leaving the terminal.

Twenty-eight boarding gates serve the main terminal, which was expanded in 2006 along with twenty-two new boarding bridges. For lounge access, the Copa Club is run jointly by Copa and United and takes Star Alliance members, and The Lounge Panama is operated by Global Lounge Network. The American Airlines Admirals Club closed in 2012, so do not send clients looking for it.

It is a working connecting airport rather than a destination in itself, and anyone on a long layover should expect to spend it airside.
after:
The main gateway for Panama City is built around connections rather than arrivals. Copa Airlines runs its hub here, and the route map fans out across the Caribbean and North, Central and South America, with some flights to Europe. That makes Tocumen one of the more useful places in the region to change planes, and the airport counted 74 per cent of its August 2026 passengers as transfers.

There are two terminals, and the airport's departures board shows Copa flights leaving from both, so check which one a connection uses. A free shuttle bus links them in a few minutes, the airport says. Lounges include the Copa Club and The Lounge Panama, run by Global Lounge Network.

Line 2 of the Panama Metro runs from a station at the airport into the city.

claims.claim: many passengers pass through without ever leaving the terminal
claims.wasBefore: and many passengers pass through without ever leaving the terminal
claims.why: Replaced by the airport's own transfer share, attributed (see above). 'Without ever leaving the terminal' no longer fits an airport of two terminals joined by a shuttle bus.

claims.claim: 28 gates in the main terminal, expanded in 2006 with 22 new boarding bridges
claims.wasBefore: Twenty-eight boarding gates serve the main terminal, which was expanded in 2006 along with twenty-two new boarding bridges.
claims.why: Out of date: Terminal 2 has been in service since 2022 (Wikipedia; the operator's pages show both terminals in use, with Terminal 1 gates numbered to at least 130 and Terminal 2 gates from 201 to 220), so 28 gates in the main terminal no longer describes the airport. The 2006 figures rest on Wikipedia alone. Replaced by the two terminals (see above).

claims.claim: Copa Club run jointly by Copa and United, taking Star Alliance members
claims.wasBefore: the Copa Club is run jointly by Copa and United and takes Star Alliance members
claims.why: Wikipedia alone: copaair.com is behind a bot check and Star Alliance's site refused, and neither the operator nor Priority Pass says who runs the Copa Club or who may use it. The Copa Club itself is kept (see above).

claims.claim: the Admirals Club closed in 2012
claims.wasBefore: The American Airlines Admirals Club closed in 2012, so do not send clients looking for it.
claims.why: The 2012 date rests on Wikipedia alone. The operator's current list of lounges (two Copa Clubs, The Lounge, a Global Lounge and the Tocumen Royal Saloon) and Priority Pass's list name no Admirals Club, and the lounge sentence now says what is there.
